text_blocks.snippet: Sleeping sickness, also known as African trypanosomiasis, is a parasitic disease transmitted by tsetse flies in sub-Saharan Africa. It's caused by Trypanosoma parasites, and without prompt treatment, it can be fatal as the parasites invade the central nervous system.
snippet_highlighted_words: a parasitic disease transmitted by tsetse flies in sub-Saharan Africa

list.snippet: Causative Agent: Trypanosoma parasites, specifically Trypanosoma brucei gambiense (chronic form, 94% of cases) and Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense (acute form, 6% of cases).
Transmission: Tsetse flies (Glossina spp.) transmit the parasites through their bites.
Geographic Distribution: Primarily found in remote, sub-Saharan African regions.

Symptoms: Early symptoms include fever, headache, swollen lymph nodes, and joint pain. As the disease progresses, neurological symptoms like sleep cycle disturbances, confusion, and sensory disturbances appear.
Progression: Untreated, the disease can lead to seizures, coma, and eventually death.
